title: Generic polynomial formal fibres over complete local domains
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian complete local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $q$ a maximal ideal of $A[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] contracting to the maximal ideal of $A$. The generic formal fibre $\kappa(0)\otimes_{A[x]}(A[x]_q)^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is geometrically regular over $\kappa(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 07PV, paragraphs 3--5, restricted to the zero prime; uses 032D, 07PP(1), 07NF, 07NY, 07PR.

proof.text: Choose A₀ with regular-local structure, finite A₀-module A, maximal-ideal contraction and a field/Cohen power-series presentation using 032D. Polynomial finiteness follows from Module.Finite.base_change and Algebra.IsPushout.equiv for the polynomial pushout. The finite polynomial algebra is integral; contract q to a maximal ideal q₀ and use mapRingHom_comp_C to identify q₀ ∩ A₀ with the maximal ideal of A₀.

For an injective finite map of Noetherian domains R → S, Mathlib Algebra.QuasiFinite supplies Artinian residue-field fibres and their discrete prime spectra. Therefore Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime holds at q. Apply formal-fibre quasi-finite ascent to 0 ⊆ q. Ideal.comap_bot_of_injective identifies the contracted generic prime with zero; substitute this equality together with the prime instance. Apply this proved private helper to A₀[X] → A[X].

For a characteristic-zero regular local domain B, Mathlib Polynomial.isRegularLocalRing_localization_atPrime_of_comap_eq_maximalIdeal makes B[X]_(q₀) regular local. Its completion C is Noetherian and regular local, and thus regular. IsLocalization.tensor identifies C tensor_(B[X]) κ(0) as localization at the images of the nonzero elements of B[X]. Apply localization-of-regular-ring using the explicit unit, fraction and kernel witnesses from IsLocalization. Exchange tensor factors to obtain the displayed generic fibre. Its residue field has characteristic zero; IsPurelyInseparable.bijective_algebraMap_of_isSeparable and includeRight_bijective identify every purely inseparable tensor base change with this regular ring. This proves both conjuncts of geometric regularity.

In the field power-series presentation, split the characteristic of k using CharP.exists'. In characteristic zero, transport CharZero through the injective constant map into the power-series ring and the presentation isomorphism, and apply the previous step. In positive characteristic p, compose MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv for Fin 1 with Polynomial.mapEquiv of the inverse coefficient presentation. Apply 07PR with m = 1 at the contraction of q₀. The same finite-ascent helper from step 2, applied to this ring isomorphism with its induced algebra structure, transports this geometric regularity to A₀[X]. Its domain and Noetherian instances transport from A₀[X] along the isomorphism.

A Cohen ring has an irreducible prime-number uniformizer p by the DVR uniformizer criterion. If its characteristic is a positive prime l, then l = p makes the uniformizer zero, contradicting irreducibility; l ≠ p makes p a unit by CharP.isUnit_natCast_iff, also contradicting irreducibility. Thus it has characteristic zero. Transport this to its power-series ring and then A₀, and apply step 3. Together with the field case and finite ascent this proves the original claim.

proof_origin.place: Proof of Proposition 07PV, generic-prime case: reduction by 032D and 07PP(1), characteristic-zero completion/localization argument, and positive-characteristic 07PR with one polynomial variable. K3 implementation uses Mathlib polynomial-localization regularity and uses finite quasi-finite ascent also for the presentation isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem completeLocalGenericFibre
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    (q : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [q.IsMaximal]
    (hq : q.comap (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular (⊥ : Ideal (Polynomial A)).ResidueField
      ((⊥ : Ideal (Polynomial A)).Fiber
        (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
          (Localization.AtPrime q)))
